chief_complaint: Management of hypertension with low current blood pressure and associated metabolic risk factors (obesity, prediabetes) plus anemia and chronic sinusitis.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 45-year-old woman with long‑standing essential hypertension diagnosed in 2005, currently treated with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Recent vital signs show a systolic/diastolic pressure of 96/57 mmHg, suggesting possible overtreatment. She has obesity (BMI ≥30) documented since 2002, prediabetes (A1c 6.2%) since 2021, and anemia of unclear etiology also since 2021. Chronic sinusitis has been present since 2020 with prior acute bacterial and viral episodes. Socially, she reports a history of intimate‑partner abuse, limited social contact, low educational attainment, and full‑time employment. She uses a levonorgestrel intrauterine system for contraception. No emergency or inpatient visits have occurred, but she has had numerous outpatient and wellness visits. Several preventive measures (statin, metformin, iron studies) are absent.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple episodes of acute and viral sinusitis (2019‑2020), acute infective cystitis (2019), prior unhealthy alcohol use (resolved 2022), resolved stress (2022), and several medication review reminders. No chronic respiratory, cardiac, or renal diseases beyond those listed as active.
